summary: The proof is sequentially valid. The positive singleton cell areas make each K_i a full-dimensional planar convex body; the affine sum excludes a common point; the exact-cell convention gives |K_i|=k-c_i; the crossing equalities give the stated uniform area lower bound; and Scott's theorem applies with coefficient 9/5. The resulting inequality M+m-k >= 93/14 contradicts M <= m+k at m=12/7. Boundary sets lie on nonconstant affine cutting lines and therefore have zero planar area.
